title: Reconstructing the 2016 withdrawal of the sacks adjustment

sources.title: Wheatland Tube Co. v. United States, Slip Op.14-137
sources.issuing_body: US Court of International Trade; Judge Leo M. Gordon
sources.reading_scope: Complete 30-page opinion, including notes, read from local extraction in consecutive bounded segments. Page29 visually checked.
sources.decisive_locators: Pages18–23 reject claims that the statute unambiguously assigns the burden only to China or forbids indirect evidence; pages24–30 require further explanation of contrary pricing evidence.
sources.limits: This is the circular-welded-pipe litigation, not the later sacks remand. Court reasoning is not a WTO compliance ruling. Underlying party briefs and exhibits were not acquired. No current statement of US judicial-review doctrine is inferred from the historical Chevron discussion.

sources.title: Redetermination Pursuant to Court Remand, Laminated Woven Sacks Committee v. United States, Court No.12-00301
sources.issuing_body: US Department of Commerce; Paul Piquado
sources.document_date: 2016-03-23 issuance reported in Federal Register; signed page visibly dated March21
sources.source_type: Primary agency remand decision, preserved official PDF
sources.reading_scope: All ten pages read: extracted pages1–7 and9–10; scanned page8 visually read and transcribed. Page6 visually checked as well.
sources.decisive_locators: Page1 and note3: December21,2015 questionnaires and reported absence of replies/comments/extension requests. Pages4–6: pipe-litigation sequence, revised method and exact requested example. Pages7–8: comments and denial. Pages9–10: cash-deposit table.
sources.limits: No original questionnaire, delivery record or company explanation recovered. Nonresponse is the agency's account; no motive inferred. Page3 repeats the older passage's CWP reference inside the sacks memorandum; that wording is not used as sacks-specific economic proof. Issuance, signature, court judgment and effective-date stages remain distinct.

interpretive_limit: The sequence explains the published administrative basis for withdrawing relief, not why the firms did not respond, the WTO legality of the revised duties, or their realized commercial effect.
